Optiverse X Method

Upload once. Keep every frame.

Social platforms re-encode every video you post. Optiverse X Method prepares your export so their encoder has very little left to compress, which keeps your colour, motion and detail intact on your audience's screen.

what it does

Made for cleaner, smoother motion.

Bitrate headroom

Your file is prepared well above the platform's delivery target. Its encoder doesn't need to make hard cuts, so far less detail is discarded.

Colour stays accurate

Colour information is tagged explicitly, so your grade looks the same on other people's phones.

Frame rate preserved

Your original cadence is kept from the first frame to the last, with no unwanted conversion.

Checked before you download

Every result is inspected against the settings you chose. If anything differs, you'll see it before you post.

questions

The details, explained.

The platform always re-encodes to its own delivery bitrate, so the final file isn't larger. What changes is the quality of what its encoder starts with. A high-bitrate source leaves it very little to discard, while a heavily compressed export gets compressed a second time. Optiverse X Method removes that second pass.

Short-form vertical feeds are usually the strictest, especially with fast motion, fine grain and saturated colour. That is the case Optiverse X Method is tuned for first.

No. Your footage is processed on your own device and is never sent to a server.

Nothing lost on the way up.

What Optimize does

Prepares your export so social platforms have very little left to compress. One tap, no settings.

  • Keeps every frameColour, motion and fine detail hold up after the platform re-encodes your upload.
  • Platform-ready MP4You get a clean MP4 matched to current recommended specs. Your original is never changed.
  • Stays on your deviceProcessing happens locally. Nothing is uploaded.

What Advanced does

Full manual control for when you know exactly what you want from the export.

  • Resolution, FPS and codecSet size and frame rate, and pick H.264, HEVC, AV1 or VP9.
  • Bitrate, audio and processorChoose video and audio bitrate, remove audio, and run on GPU or CPU.
  • Aspect ratio and cropReframe to 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 and more. Crop or pad, never stretched.

Runs on your device. Processor: GPU only never uses the CPU encoder, CPU only never uses the GPU. GPU only uses your device’s video chip (fastest, never falls back). CPU only uses the browser’s own software encoder. Higher FPS repeats frames, lower FPS drops frames. Leave the bitrate empty to keep about the original file size. Issued cards

Cards are saved on the server and locked to the account you pick.

Reference

How cards work

Locked to one account
A card only works for the Gmail account you picked. On any other account it is simply "not recognised". The client has to register first, then you pick the account here.
What a card does
It unlocks Compress, Patch Video and Advanced on that account, on every device. If the client wipes the phone or the browser and logs in again, the plan is still there.
Card holder
With the name lock on, the client has to type the name exactly as printed on the card (capital letters, spaces and dots do not matter). Without it, any name works.
Expiry and one-time use
A card can only be activated inside the time you pick, and the first successful activation uses it up. "Plan length" decides how long the plan lasts after that (permanent by default).
Deactivate
Deactivate kills a card at once, even after it was used: the account goes back to Free within a minute. Restore brings it back.
Sharing
Send the code, or the saved image, only to the person who bought it.

Header patcher

Patch video

Your video never leaves this device. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

What this patch does

Rewrites the frame rate and resolution values in the file header and saves a new copy. The video and audio data are copied unchanged.

  • Frame rateSets the FPS value in the timing header to 30. On by default and detected from your file. Frames are not added or removed, so the clip’s length changes with the rate.
  • ResolutionSets the width and height in the track header. Optional and off by default. The encoded pixels stay the same.
  • Credit tag“patch by teamoptiverseX” is written into the Artist, Encoder and Copyright metadata of every patched file.
  • Stays on your deviceOnly the file header is read and rewritten. Nothing leaves this page.

Frame rate is stored in the mvhd and mdhd timescales. Resolution is stored in the tkhd and the video sample entry. The credit tag is written to moov › udta › meta › ilst (Artist, Encoder, Copyright). Every other byte stays identical. Tools such as ffprobe or MediaInfo may still report the original encoded size.
